PUBLIC BUSINESS FROM THE FLOOR - AGENDIZED ITEMS
Any person who would like to address the Legislative Bodies on any agendized item is requested to complete a speaker card for the City Clerk/Agency/Authority Secretary and identify the agenda item you would like to discuss. Each person will be given an opportunity to address the Legislative Body at the time such item is discussed. Speaker cards are available at the rear of the Council Chambers and your speaker card must be filled out prior to the agenda item being called. We respectfully request that you fill the cards out completely and print as clearly as possible. Following this procedure will allow for a smooth and timely process for the meeting and we appreciate your cooperation. Individual speakers are limited to three (3) minutes each.
Consent Calendar items under the Legislative Body may be acted upon with one motion, a second and the vote. If you desire to speak on an item or items on the Consent Calendar, you may fill out one speaker card for the Consent Calendar. You will be given three minutes to address your concerns before the Legislative Body takes action on the Consent Calendar.

CC 6. Approve Resolution No. 18-43, designating those officials authorized to file applications to the California Office of Emergency Services to obtain federal and state financial assistance.
According to Public Law 93-288, as amended by the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act of 1988, it is required that the City Council now designate an authorized agent every three years to execute and file the application to the California Office of Emergency Services (CalOES) to obtain certain federal and/or state financial assistance. The universal resolution is not disaster-specific and will be kept on file by CalOES for a period of three years.

CC 7. Adopt Ordinance No. 1046, amending the zoning plan for portions of land at the northeast corner of Division Street and Avenue I, known as Zone Change No. 17-04, rezoning 0.16 acres (Assessorâ€™s Parcel Numbers 3176-005-922 and 3176-055-930) from P (Public) to S (School), and 15.6 acres (Assessorâ€™s Parcel Numbers 3176-005-918, 21 and 30) from P and S to R-7,000 (single-family residential, minimum lot size 7,000 square feet).
The proposed project would bring new single-family housing to a vacant area once occupied by the original Antelope Valley Fairgrounds. The development would be governed by a homeownersâ€™ association (HOA), which would manage the common areas, and ensure quality standards are enforced. The proposed development would improve and beautify an intersection, which will add value to the immediate area. In addition, the project would be compatible with the single-family homes, solar field, medical center, restaurant, and other service type uses that surround the proposed subject site.

CC 8. Approve the application for grant funds from the Department of Transportationâ€™s Active Transportation Program Cycle 4 Grant, Recreation Trails Section. If received, this will fund the Prime Desert Woodland Preserve Trails Expansion.
The City of Lancaster recently purchased a 20.3-acre parcel adjacent to the Prime Desert Woodland Preserve. Staff is applying for grant funds from the Department of Transportationâ€™s Active Transportation Program (ATP) Cycle 4 Grant, Recreation Trails Section to construct improvements on this additional acreage. If approved, this grant will provide funds for the development of an additional 5,500 linear feet of recreational walking trails within the Preserve and amenities, including but not limited to: benches, restrooms, water fountain, and educational panels.

Award contract to American Business Machines (ABM), the regional Canon USA authorized dealer, under the cooperative agreement for Kern County Schools PEPPM Bid #527080 with Canon USA, Inc., for a lease total of $358,571.41; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. This contract is awarded in accordance with City of Lancaster Municipal Code Chapter 3.32.
The Cityâ€™s fleet of 23 copiers/printers are at the end of their useful life and the lease is currently paid on a month-to-month basis. Staff is seeking to upgrade and consolidate these devices with newer technology at an affordable price. After an extensive review of the proposal from ABM, an evaluation committee, consisting of staff from Finance, Development Services, and Parks departments, determined, based on several criteria, that ABM would provide the best-value to the City. Additionally, ABM provided the City with a successful proposal presentation and a successful product demonstration.

CC 10. Endorse the accuracy of information presented in Lancaster Choice Energyâ€™s (LCE) 2017 Power Content Label based on staffâ€™s review and independent auditor report.
California Public Utilities Code requires all retail sellers of electric energy, including Lancaster Choice Energy (LCE), to disclose â€œaccurate, reliable, and simple-to-understand information on the sources of energyâ€ that are delivered to their respective customers. Information presented in the Power Content Label includes the appropriate share of total energy supply based on resource type, including both renewable and conventional fuel sources. To fulfill its Power Content Label reporting obligation, LCE must provide the California Energy Commission (CEC) with Councilâ€™s attestation regarding the accuracy of information included in the Power Content Label.

CC 11. Adopt Resolution No. 18-44, granting authority to the City Manager to enter into certain contracts on behalf of Lancaster Choice Energy and repealing Resolution No. 15-44.
LCE agreements often require swift execution and/or may not raise policy considerations that require LCE Board input, it is appropriate for LCE management to have discretion to execute certain short term LCE contracts. Accordingly, staff recommends that the City Council grant the City Manager authority to enter into shorter-term contracts for the procurement or sale of energy, resource adequacy capacity, and renewable energy certificates while requiring LCE Board approval for longer-term contracts.

PH 1. Appeal of Conditional Use Permit No. 18-02 for a Proposed Medical Cannabis Cultivation and Manufacturing Facility Located at 45761 Division Street
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 18-45, upholding the Planning Commissionâ€™s decision by denying the appeal for Conditional Use Permit No. 18-02 to allow for the operation and construction of a medical cannabis cultivation and manufacturing facility.
The appellant, Better Neighborhoods, Inc., filed an appeal of the Commissionâ€™s action on June 29, 2018. The applicantâ€™s appeal identifies questions and comments, and indicates that â€œadditional study is necessary on several issues to determine whether they might create significant environmental impacts resulting from the project, and whether feasible mitigation measures can be implemented that would reduce the identified significant impacts to less than a significant level.â€ The appellant did not provide any further evidence that would identify additional environmental impacts or concerns that would require further investigation; therefore, staff believes that the required information and technical studies/data provided by the applicant, along with the MND, adequately discuss all factors, and appropriately mitigates potentially significant environmental issues.

NB 1. Amending cannabis regulations
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 18-46, repealing Resolution No. 17-05 and establishing the maximum number of licenses and permits that may be issued for cultivation of medical cannabis
The City Council adopted Ordinance 1019 authorizing the cultivation and manufacture of medical cannabis within the City and Resolution 17-05 limiting the number of medical cannabis cultivation licenses pursuant to Chapter 5.56 and medical cannabis conditional use permits 17.43 on February 28, 2017. The Councilâ€™s original limitation on the number of cannabis licenses and conditional use permits allowed staff and the planning commission the opportunity to work through the licensing and permitting process in an orderly and efficient manner with a small number of applicants. Now that staff and the planning commission have successfully implemented systems to process applicants under the Ordinance, staff recommends that the Council authorize the City Manager to determine the maximum number of licenses and permits that may be issued pursuant to Chapters 5.56 and 17.43 of the Cityâ€™s Municipal Code; provided, however, that the City Manager shall report back to the City Council after each multiple of ten (10) local licenses are issued pursuant to Chapter 5.56 of the Cityâ€™s Municipal Code and ten (10) conditional use permits are issued pursuant to Chapter 17.43 of the Cityâ€™s Municipal Code.
